subject: biochemistry
title: Cholesterol and steroidogenesis: HMG-CoA reductase, statins, bile acids and adrenocortical pathways

steps.tx: All twenty-seven carbons of **cholesterol** originate from cytosolic acetyl-CoA. Two acetyl-CoAs condense to acetoacetyl-CoA, followed by condensation with a third acetyl-CoA by cytosolic HMG-CoA synthase. The rate-limiting committed step is catalyzed by HMG-CoA reductase in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, reducing HMG-CoA to mevalonate using two NADPH molecules. Statins are competitive structural analogues that potently inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, upregulating hepatic LDL receptors.
steps.say: All twenty-seven carbons of cholesterol derive from acetyl-CoA. Cytosolic HMG-CoA synthase generates HMG-CoA. The rate-limiting step is HMG-CoA reductase, which reduces HMG-CoA to mevalonate using two NADPH. Statins competitively inhibit this enzyme, lowering intracellular cholesterol and upregulating hepatic LDL receptors.

steps.tx: Cholesterol homeostasis is governed by **SREBP-2**, the sterol regulatory element-binding protein. In sterol-replete cells, SREBP-2 is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum bound to SCAP and Insig. When intracellular sterol concentrations decline, Insig dissociates, allowing SCAP to chaperone SREBP-2 to the Golgi apparatus. Two site-specific proteases cleave the active basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, which translocates to the nucleus to induce transcription of LDL receptors.
steps.say: SREBP-2 regulates cholesterol synthesis and uptake. When cholesterol is plentiful, SREBP-2 is anchored in the ER by SCAP and Insig. When cholesterol drops, SCAP shuttles SREBP-2 to the Golgi for proteolytic release. The active domain enters the nucleus to induce LDL receptor and reductase genes.

steps.tx: Hepatic conversion into **bile acids** represents the primary quantitative pathway for cholesterol elimination. Cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting initial hydroxylation, forming primary bile acids: cholic acid and chenodeoxycholic acid. These are conjugated with glycine or taurine to form amphipathic bile salts. Intestinal bacteria deconjugate and 7-dehydroxylate them into secondary bile acids (deoxycholic acid and lithocholic acid), ninety-five percent of which are reabsorbed via the terminal ileum.
steps.say: Converting cholesterol into bile acids provides the primary route for cholesterol excretion. Cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting step, producing primary bile acids. Conjugation with glycine or taurine forms bile salts. Intestinal bacteria generate secondary bile acids, ninety-five percent recycled by the terminal ileum.

steps.tx: Steroidogenesis in the adrenal cortex and gonads begins with **StAR**-mediated cholesterol import into the mitochondrial matrix. Desmolase (CYP11A1) cleaves the side chain to yield pregnenolone, the universal steroid precursor. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia most commonly results from twenty-one-hydroxylase deficiency, which blocks cortisol and aldosterone synthesis. This shunts accumulated precursors into adrenal androgens, causing virilization and life-threatening salt wasting.
steps.say: Steroidogenesis begins with StAR protein transporting cholesterol into mitochondrial matrix, where CYP11A1 cleaves it to pregnenolone. The most common form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia is 21-hydroxylase deficiency, blocking cortisol and aldosterone, shunting precursors to androgens and causing ambiguous genitalia and salt wasting.

rows: Ambiguous genitalia in females, salt loss
